name: Action-cue tension with metric modulation: tempo map from sync-point markers, 100 BPM 4/4 to quarter-note triplet = 150 BPM, 3/4 -> 6/8 -> 5/8 (truncate an eighth), dotted-eighth = 133 BPM, return to tempo primo; piano sketch with ostinatos from one motif, then an edited MIDI rhythm track and orchestration by role
goal: Turn one simple motif into a minute of escalating action music by changing tempo and meter smoothly instead of randomly: mark sync points, then use metric modulation (a subdivision of the old beat becomes the new beat) plus time-signature changes to hit them, sketch on piano with ostinatos and motif variations, build a temp rhythm track from loop MIDI that you edit (accents, rests), and orchestrate with low ostinatos, supporting winds/brass and a percussive piano.

source.title: Build tension for your action cue: Metric modulation, time signature changes, ostinatos and more !

prerequisites: DAW with a tempo/signature track and markers
Piano and any orchestral or synth ensemble sounds; a rhythm-loop instrument that can export MIDI

inputs.name: sync_points
inputs.description: Times (s or SMPTE) the music must hit

outputs.name: cue
outputs.description: ~1-minute cue with a tempo map of metric modulations hitting the sync points

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Tempo changes follow metric relationships (new tempo = old tempo x subdivision ratio), not arbitrary jumps.
Edit loop MIDI (accents, rests, notes) so the rhythm track is not a stock loop.
Synth voices keep steady pitch (no random wobble).
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Set a starting tempo and meter (e.g. 100 BPM, 4/4) and place markers at each sync point.
Metric modulation up: let the quarter-note triplet of the old tempo become the new beat (100 x 3/2 = 150 BPM).
Change meters to fit sync points and add drive: 3/4 -> 6/8, then 5/8 by truncating one eighth note.
Modulate again: make the dotted eighth of the old tempo the new quarter (100 / 0.75 = ~133 BPM); finally return to the opening tempo (tempo primo) to end the cycle.
Piano sketch over the tempo map: derive ostinatos and simple variations from the motif.
Temp rhythm track: export loop MIDI into the DAW and edit accents, rests and notes so it fits your sections.

Orchestrate by role: replace the piano opening with a harp-like plucked voice, double low ostinatos in low strings/bass synth, use winds to support and brass (the loudest section) for key dynamic points; bring piano back as a percussive ostinato; add clusters/effects at the opening.

verification: Every tempo change can be written as old BPM x ratio (3/2, 4/3...).
Section boundaries line up with the sync-point markers.
The motif is recognisable in at least two variations.
